thread:
maria: quick design check — we keep hitting weird perm mismatches when an org-scoped API key is allowed to call multiple project services. thinking about a gateway canonicalization step: convert incoming api key -> canonical principal + short-lived caller token, then propagate only the caller token and per-route entitlements. avoids leaking api-key scopes downstream. anyone see obvious downside?

kevin: +1 on canonicalization. main downside is extra token minting latency on hot paths. measurable?

sam: we measured minting time in a spike last quarter — ~12ms p95 for our lightweight signer (when warm). batching helps but not always applicable.

irene: also watch ops surface: now every downstream must accept ephemeral tokens and call introspection or validate JWTs. thats more rollout friction.

maria: good point. idea: gateway mints JWT with minimal claims (sub, aud, exp, entitlements) signed by internal KMS key, and downstream validate locally (no introspect). avoids rps to auth service.

kevin: local validation is nice. but key rotation / key distribution becomes critical. we can rotate keys via a short TTL public key bundle cached in services (similar to OIDC jwks).

jordan: question — do we still need to carry original api key id for audit? i.e. add x-original-key: key-id in telemetry but not for auth decisions.

maria: yes, keep key-id for logs only. do NOT use it for auth checks. that prevents accidental policy expansion downstream.

sam: small nit: some legacy jobs embed api keys in headers now and call internal admin routes. migrating them to ephemeral tokens might be tedious. plan migration path?

irene: migration plan: 1) backward-compat gateway accepts both; 2) emit deprecation telemetry; 3) block high-risk endpoints first; 4) require ephemeral-only for new internal routes.

auth-bot: deploy-check — can add mint-service to canary with 5% traffic. will emit metrics: mint_latency_ms, jwt_sign_errors, jwt_validations_failed.

kevin: operational cost: we should quantify token throughput and KMS signing QPS. if signer becomes bottleneck we can add local HSM cache or sign with short-lived signing key rotated frequently.

maria: agreed. next steps: i'll write a short RFC proposing canonicalize-at-gateway + jwt propagation + key-bundle validation. include migration plan and perf targets (mint p95 <25ms). anyone want to volunteer for spike to measure signer + jwks cache hit rates?

sam: i'll run the spike this week and post numbers.

irene: i'll draft rollout steps and deprecation policy for legacy jobs.

jordan: i'll add an audit schema for original-key metadata and make sure it's excluded from runtime auth decisions.

maria: thanks — will open the RFC and link here. :thumbsup:
